# Nerio

Nerio is an open-source, source-first design system for modern digital products. It is universal and domain-agnostic: suitable for SaaS applications, consumer products, marketplaces, dashboards, internal tools, content platforms, creator tools, productivity products, and data-rich workflows.

Nerio has two product layers: Nerio Core and Nerio Pro.

Nerio Core is the open-source foundation: tokens, themes, primitive and base UI components, public docs, public registry, CLI, and public MCP/component discovery.

Nerio Pro is the paid advanced layer: complex product components, templates, premium themes, Figma assets, advanced registry items, and Pro MCP/AI tooling.

Core = building blocks. Pro = product-ready solutions.

The canonical Core UI implementation and review standard is `docs/core-ui-best-practices.md`. Apply
its four-owner model: the maintainer owns visual-language values and character, Core owns reusable
technical primitive contracts, consumers own application policy and composition, and Pro owns
reusable product-ready workflows. Before adding a prop, variant, size, state, slot, event, or
imperative handle, prefer existing composition, semantic/component tokens, consumer `className` or
source ownership, and meaningful slots in that order. Admit public API only for a stable,
domain-agnostic semantic or behavioral need with multiple independent use cases, preserved
accessibility and entrypoint boundaries, and justified maintenance cost. Classify styling decisions
as system rules, family rules, or reasoned component exceptions.

The maintainer-approved Nerio 1.0 visual language is documented in
`docs/visual-language-1-0.md`, with recurring inconsistencies grouped by system cause in
`docs/audits/visual-language-1-0.md`. It is the implementation-ready art-direction contract for
color and surfaces, typography, geometry and spacing, interaction states, motion, iconography, and
signature details. It does not introduce a new runtime axis or silently change public APIs.

Public component documentation lives under `/docs`. `/blocks` is the metadata-driven catalog for
bounded product tasks, while `/templates` is the catalog for complete app-like scenarios. Their
same-origin full-screen previews live under `/views/blocks/[slug]` and `/views/[slug]`. Internal
stress fixtures live under unindexed `/visual-test/blocks/[slug]` routes and are not public Blocks.
Operations Workspace proves complete product composition but is not a released Pro package or
stable distribution surface. Finance & Assets adds a deterministic consolidated portfolio,
holdings, transaction, transfer-review, and security/display scenario at
`/views/finance-assets`. It uses the optional
charts adapter and local mock data only; it is not a released financial product, backend, or Pro
package. These are the only current Templates; additional scenarios will be rebuilt before they
return to the catalog.

The public Foundations index is `/docs/foundations/tokens`, `/docs/foundations/color`,
`/docs/foundations/typography`, `/docs/foundations/spacing-layout`,
`/docs/foundations/themes`, `/docs/foundations/accessibility`,
`/docs/foundations/localization`, `/docs/foundations/radius`,
`/docs/foundations/effects`, `/docs/foundations/motion`, and
`/docs/foundations/icons`. These canonical routes share one typed
discovery projection used by navigation, documentation search, adjacent-page links, and the sitemap.

The legacy `/docs/foundations/animations` URL redirects permanently to the canonical Motion
foundation and does not compete in navigation, search, the sitemap, or this index.
Source-backed Typography, Themes, and Color tables are generated from the canonical token CSS and
runtime catalog; editorial guidance remains hand-authored. Color guidance uses semantic roles,
evaluates complete foreground/background and interaction-state sequences, keeps meaning available
without hue, and validates custom themes in light, dark, system-dark, forced-colors, and real
component contexts.

Spacing and layout guidance renders the primitive spacing scale, density aliases, and representative
component geometry from the same source-backed projection. Core owns those contracts and resilient
component behavior; products own page grids, breakpoints, application shells, routing layouts,
content priority, and domain hierarchy. Compact density remaps semantic and component aliases
without redefining primitive spacing, shrinking content indiscriminately, or adding another runtime
axis.

Direction and localization use one Core 1.1 contract. HTML `dir` owns layout and CSS inheritance;
direction-sensitive Base UI primitives receive the same value through
`@base-ui/react/direction-provider`. Nerio does not add a direction runtime axis or locale provider.
Calendar and DatePicker default to explicit `en-US` formatting for deterministic server/client
markup, while consumer applications own translation catalogs, routing, product copy, currencies,
time zones, and domain formatting.

Use `/docs/changelog` for notable Nerio releases and project announcements. Follow the official
Nerio account at `https://x.com/nerio_ui` for release notes, component updates, documentation
improvements, and important project news. The repository `CHANGELOG.md` remains the canonical
technical history.

Data Display and Feedback follow one neutral-first hierarchy. Card is a generic raised white or
black surface with a soft shadow and no default border; secondary grouping and TableContainer use
flat muted surfaces. Table keeps native semantics and consumer-owned behavior while selected or
current rows combine a neutral fill with a logical-edge indicator. Avatar fallbacks use fixed
light/dark fills and overlap borders so translucent seams do not appear in groups. Alert is a flat
muted inline surface whose semantic tone is carried by its icon and complete message text. Toast is
an adaptive raised overlay surface with standard mode-aware text and controls, subtle elevation,
and restrained semantic status icons. Stat trend text is neutral by default because Core does not
infer direction or meaning from an arbitrary string.

Navigation, Layout, and Overlays use one focus, selection, and motion language. Current navigation
stays neutral unless a compact indicator is needed; segmented Tabs use a soft selected-surface
shadow, and hover feedback resolves through shared motion tokens. Popover, Dropdown Menu, Command,
Dialog, Sheet, and Toast use standard adaptive overlay surfaces and text hierarchy; compact popups
use smaller radii than Dialog and Sheet. Tooltip remains the dark-glass exception in every mode.
Modal backdrops blur, Dialog settles
with restrained scale and opacity, and Sheet preserves the physical direction of its side. Dialog
and Sheet titles render neutral 16 px `div` elements by default with explicit heading opt-in, while
their descriptions use the standard 14 px body size. Their close controls are secondary icon
Buttons, while their action footers align to the inline end. Sidebar and Command remain low-level
primitives without routing, persistence, or product search policy.

Dialog preserves its convenience API and also exposes compound Root, Trigger, Portal, Backdrop,
Content, Header, Title, Description, Body, Footer, and Close parts. Use AlertDialog for destructive
or difficult-to-reverse confirmation: Base UI supplies alertdialog semantics and disables pointer
dismissal, Cancel is the recommended initial-focus target, and consumer code owns mutation,
permissions, routing, error recovery, and confirmation copy.

Dropdown Menu preserves its trigger-and-items convenience API and also exposes compound Root,
Trigger, Portal, Positioner, Content, Group, GroupLabel, Item, LinkItem, CheckboxItem, RadioGroup,
RadioItem, Submenu, SubTrigger, SubContent, Separator, ItemLabel, ItemDescription, and Shortcut
parts. Use action items for commands, link items for navigation, checkbox items for independent
settings, and radio groups for one-of-many choices. Core owns accessible interaction and bounded
positioning, while routing, permissions, analytics, command execution, and confirmation policy
remain consumer-owned. ContextMenu, Menubar, and NavigationMenu are separate non-goals.

Use `COMPONENTS.md` and `data/component-catalog.json` as the source of truth for Core/Pro component tiering.

Core `1.0.0-beta.1` is the current public beta; all six public packages resolve from npm under both `beta` and `latest`, while protected `alpha` remains on `0.1.0-alpha.2`. Public package, Registry, CLI, MCP, and clean-consumer verification passed, while the external-feedback gate and manual accessibility/device evidence remain pending before stable 1.0. The Core 1.0 contract is frozen through a reviewed machine-readable snapshot spanning package exports and types, tokens, Registry, CLI, MCP, support ranges, and public docs routes. Temporary alpha compatibility aliases are removed; all current Core components use their canonical APIs. Pro components remain outside Core. Command Primitive owns the accessible query field, local or consumer-filtered leaf results, sound flat or grouped collections, active option, disabled navigation, selection events, and empty/loading presentation. Keyword and stable-value text affect matching only; selection writes the visible label to the controlled or uncontrolled query and form value while `onSelect` emits the stable value. CommandItem leading content owns its accessibility semantics, while decorative Nerio Icons hide themselves. Command does not own fetching, ranking, routing, global shortcuts, recent/history storage, analytics, permissions, or a complete command palette. Sidebar Primitive owns layout, physical side, controlled or uncontrolled collapse state, regions, and accessible toggles; it does not own routes, navigation data, menus, permissions, persistence, or AppShell behavior. Compose Sheet explicitly for mobile and render one interactive navigation tree per viewport. Sheet is a stable Base UI modal side-panel primitive with explicit left/right/top/bottom sides, sm/md/lg sizes, neutral SheetClose composition, a safe-area-aware default close, shared enter/exit motion contracts, compound slots, and no app navigation or settings behavior. Dialog keeps its icon close control localizable through `closeLabel` while preserving the default accessible name. RadioGroup supports concise data-driven `options` and compositional `RadioGroupItem` children; use composition for richer option content. A Core component should not move to `stable-core` until its API, accessibility, tokens, registry metadata, docs, CLI fixture, MCP metadata, and validation checks are aligned.

Use `/docs/feedback` for the public feedback path. Core 1.0 beta reports begin in the canonical release discussion at `https://github.com/vpavlov-me/Nerio/discussions/385`; browse Ideas and Q&A through `https://github.com/vpavlov-me/Nerio/discussions`. Public comments inform the external-feedback gate but do not replace recorded independent-consumer, manual accessibility, or physical-device evidence.

Use primitive tokens only for raw values. Use semantic tokens such as `--n-color-surface-default`, `--n-color-text-primary`, `--n-color-action-primary`, `--n-color-border-default`, `--n-font-sans`, and `--n-font-mono` in product code. Components should prefer component tokens for local contracts such as `--n-button-background-primary`, `--n-input-border`, `--n-dialog-width-md`, `--n-overlay-background`, and `--n-table-cell-padding-x`.

Nerio is neutral-first and compact: use white or black primary surfaces, cool blue-gray grouping fills, whitespace between major blocks, restrained internal spacing, regular 12-14px UI typography, large concentric radii, and borderless controls by default. Adaptive controls, hover and pressed states, neutral selected surfaces, subdued borders, and grid lines use cool near-black alpha primitives in light mode and white alpha primitives in dark mode so the same semantic layer composes naturally over different surfaces. Canvas, primary surfaces, text, actions, semantic status colors, chart series, and contrast-critical roles remain opaque. Reserve the brand color for primary actions, focus, and compact justified selection indicators. Transient overlays use standard adaptive surface, text, control, border, and elevation tokens; Tooltip and chart tooltips alone retain the inverted black-glass token family. Placeholders may provide the compact visual prompt only when an explicit accessible name remains present.

System UI is the default Core font stack and the cross-platform system mono stack is the default technical font. Geist is the documentation brand only. Core provides System, Geist, Inter, IBM Plex, Manrope, Source Sans 3, and Space Grotesk scoped token recipes; non-system families remain consumer-loaded, no font files are bundled, and components must consume font tokens rather than hard-coded families.

Nerio separates theme, mode, and density. Theme is selected with `data-theme="purple"`, `data-theme="blue"`, `data-theme="green"`, `data-theme="orange"`, `data-theme="red"`, `data-theme="neutral"`, or a custom product theme. Mode is selected with `data-mode="system"`, `data-mode="light"`, or `data-mode="dark"`. Density is selected with `data-density="comfortable"` or `data-density="compact"`.

Primitive tokens are immutable raw values across theme, mode, and density selectors. Runtime selectors remap semantic and component contracts instead. The docs header exposes System, Light, and Dark through one compact icon menu, follows OS preference changes while System is selected, and restores appearance before hydration.

Default runtime attributes: `data-theme="purple" data-mode="system" data-density="comfortable"`.

Do not create or use combined theme names such as `purple-light`, `purple-dark`, `neutral-light`, `neutral-dark`, `blue-light`, `blue-dark`, `red-light`, or `red-dark`. Do not create vertical-specific Core preset names such as `fintech-blue`; use generic brand color names.

Font, radius, motion, spacing, shadow/elevation, and contrast are token-customizable in v1, but they are not separate runtime axes. Do not introduce `data-font`, `data-radius`, `data-motion`, `data-contrast`, or `data-scale` unless a later architecture decision explicitly promotes them. Typography presets are CSS token recipes, not runtime attributes; customize typography with `--n-font-sans`, `--n-font-mono`, `--n-font-sans-system`, and scoped product overrides.

Brand color is a restrained accent. Use it for primary actions, selection, active states, focus, links, small progress signals, the primary chart series, and brand moments. Do not use brand color for broad page backgrounds, routine icons, card backgrounds, standard borders, or secondary actions.

The Nerio 1.0 foundation uses pure white light foundations, pure black dark foundations, cool
alpha-neutral adaptive layers, generous role-based radii, compact 14px typography, and tokenized
motion. Use opaque neutrals for contrast-critical or overlap-isolated geometry such as Avatar
boundaries. Use semantic surface and border aliases instead of consuming alpha primitives directly.
The maintainer implementation reference is `docs/visual-language-1-0.md` in the source repository.

Core motion remains CSS-first. Install `motion` and use the optional client-only
`@nerio-ui/adapters/motion` entrypoint only for coordinated presence, interruption, layout
continuity, gestures, or product-level sequencing. `NerioMotionConfig` follows the user's reduced
motion preference; the preferred loading path is strict `LazyMotion` plus `m` and
`domAnimation`, with `domMax` reserved for layout, pan, or drag. Unrelated adapters and
`@nerio-ui/ui` resolve no Motion runtime. The stable adapter exports `NerioMotionConfig`,
`useNerioReducedMotion`, `motionTransitions`, and `motionVariants`; the config accepts only
`children`, an optional CSP `nonce`, and deterministic-test `skipAnimations`.

Prefer composition, explicit slots, semantic HTML, visible focus states, and accessible labels. Use Nerio's icon adapter for Lucide or custom SVG React components.

Card anatomy is `Card`, optional `CardVisual`, `CardHeader`, `CardTitle`, `CardDescription`, optional `CardAction`, `CardContent`, and `CardFooter`. `CardTitle` renders a neutral `div` by default and accepts an explicit `as="h2"` through `as="h6"` only when the card belongs in the document outline. `CardDescription` uses the standard 14 px body size. `CardHeader` owns the title-description gap, including the standard title wrapper used beside `CardAction`. `CardVisual` accepts generic visual content and only supports `inset` or `bleed` placement. `CardAction` is for surface Cards only; linked Cards must not contain interactive descendants.

Package entrypoints: import static Core components and utilities from `@nerio-ui/ui`, interactive components from `@nerio-ui/ui/client`, styles from `@nerio-ui/ui/styles.css`, and icons or icon types from `@nerio-ui/adapters/icons`. The adapter package has no aggregating root export; optional integrations use `@nerio-ui/adapters/table`, `@nerio-ui/adapters/charts`, `@nerio-ui/adapters/forms`, or `@nerio-ui/adapters/schema` with the matching peer installed. Core packages ship TypeScript source, so Next.js consumers list the Nerio packages they use in `transpilePackages`. SidebarHeader, SidebarContent, SidebarFooter, SidebarInset, and Icon are server-safe; SidebarProvider, Sidebar, SidebarTrigger, SidebarRail, and useSidebar import from the client entrypoint. SidebarContent forwards an HTMLDivElement ref, SidebarInset preserves stable div or main refs, and SidebarRail stays bottom-right inside its bounded hit area. Example: `import { Settings } from "@nerio-ui/adapters/icons"; import { Alert, Breadcrumbs, Card, Field, Icon, List, Pagination, SidebarContent, SidebarInset, Table } from "@nerio-ui/ui"; import { Button, Calendar, DatePicker, Select, Slider, Dialog, Sheet, Sidebar, SidebarProvider, SidebarRail, ToastProvider } from "@nerio-ui/ui/client"; import "@nerio-ui/ui/styles.css";`. Use Button's `link` variant with a native anchor render target for text-level navigation. Source-installed registry components keep local paths such as `@/components/nerio/components/button`; `nerio init` defaults to `src/components/nerio` for projects with `src/app` or `src/pages`, matching the standard Next.js `@/*` alias, and otherwise defaults to `components/nerio`.

Collapsible and Accordion are client-only Core 1.1 disclosure primitives. Collapsible owns one controlled or uncontrolled open panel. Accordion owns an array of stable string item values, defaults to single expansion, and enables independent open items with `multiple`. Both use Base UI native button triggers, stable trigger-panel relationships, disabled state, tokenized measured-height motion, density aliases, RTL-safe logical layout, forced-colors focus, and immediate reduced-motion state changes. AccordionHeader defaults to `h3`; use render composition to select the heading level required by the surrounding document outline. Closed panels unmount by default so hidden interactive descendants leave the focus order; use `keepMounted` or `hiddenUntilFound` only when persistence or browser page search requires browser-hidden content. Plain native `details` and `summary` remain the preferred zero-abstraction path for simple uncontrolled disclosure. Routing, FAQ schema, fetching, nested persistence, analytics, and product workflows remain consumer-owned.

Registry usage: install the coordinated local tools with `pnpm add -D @nerio-ui/registry@1.0.0-beta.1 @nerio-ui/cli@1.0.0-beta.1`. The canonical local workflow is `pnpm exec nerio init`, `pnpm exec nerio list`, `pnpm exec nerio info button`, `pnpm exec nerio add button --dry-run`, `pnpm exec nerio add button`, `pnpm exec nerio diff button`, `pnpm exec nerio update button --dry-run`, and `pnpm exec nerio doctor`. Init creates `nerio.json` with the immutable `@nerio-ui/registry/manifest.json` package Registry by default, defaults the component directory to `src/components/nerio` when `src/app` or `src/pages` exists and to `components/nerio` otherwise, and accepts explicit component-directory, local filesystem, and HTTP overrides. List prints component names, titles, and categories, info shows Registry metadata, and add installs the selected source item plus its dependency closure. A successful install writes portable `nerio.lock.json` metadata with the Registry schema/version/revision, style contract, requested items, installed paths, dependency closure, and original SHA-256 hashes; it stores no source content, secrets, or absolute paths. Diff classifies unchanged, local, upstream, added, removed, and conflicting drift, while update with `--dry-run` previews an upgrade. A normal update applies only safe upstream changes and never overwrites locally modified source silently; resolve conflicts manually or use `--force` only as an intentional replacement. Doctor diagnoses incompatible Registry/CLI/schema versions, missing or stale installed metadata, missing Registry or npm dependencies, token/style contract drift, mixed package/source mode, source modifications, Tailwind setup, and legacy CSS, while distinguishing blocking errors from informational drift. Use `pnpm dlx @nerio-ui/cli@1.0.0-beta.1 init` or `pnpm dlx @nerio-ui/cli@1.0.0-beta.1 add button` only for intentional one-off execution; prefer the local install for repeatable lifecycle work.

The removed alpha `IconButton` export migrates to `Button` icon-only mode: `<Button icon={Settings} aria-label="Workspace settings" />`. Other alpha replacements are Button `subtle` to `secondary`, Button `destructive` to `danger`, Badge `variant` to `tone`, Badge `icon` to `leadingIcon`, Select and RadioGroup `onChange` to `onValueChange`, Pagination item `"aria-label"` to `ariaLabel`, and List `ordered` to `marker="decimal"`. The public migration page is `/docs/migration`.

Icon owns decorative or meaningful ARIA semantics and keeps every SVG non-focusable. Custom SVG components implement generic `IconSvgProps`; use `lucideAbsoluteStrokeWidth` only for Lucide fixed-stroke behavior. Item and ItemGroup compose refs already attached to `render` elements with forwarded refs. Pagination preserves `data-current` for static current pages without `href` or `onSelect`. TableContainer creates a focusable region only for `focusable={true}` plus a non-empty runtime `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`; Table row states apply only to `tbody`, and `aria-current="false"` remains neutral.

The read-only MCP server uses the official Model Context Protocol stdio transport. Install it with `pnpm add -D @nerio-ui/mcp@1.0.0-beta.1`, then configure the MCP client with command `pnpm` and arguments `["exec", "nerio-mcp"]`; one-off clients may use command `pnpm` and arguments `["dlx", "@nerio-ui/mcp@1.0.0-beta.1"]`. The packaged server reads its version from coordinated package metadata and requires no monorepo path. Its tools are `get_registry`, `list_components`, `get_component`, and `get_component_usage`; all responses come from the same versioned Nerio Registry metadata used by the CLI. Every tool declares an output schema and returns equivalent structured content and formatted JSON text; missing components use the stable `COMPONENT_NOT_FOUND` error code. `get_registry` returns the Registry schema, release version, exact source revision, and style contract. `get_component_usage` returns usage, dependencies, registry dependencies, install files, Base UI primitives, slots, variants, states, required tokens, and accessibility guidance.

Registry `requiredTokens` should expose public customization points, preferably component aliases rather than internal implementation details. Registry `requiredTokens` and public component reference token chips must point to real `--n-*` CSS variables in `@nerio-ui/tokens`; `pnpm validate:docs` checks this contract.

Progress is a server-safe Core component for completion of one task that takes time. It requires exactly one accessible name through a visible `label`, `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby`; finite values are clamped within normalized `min` and `max` range values, while indeterminate Progress omits `aria-valuenow`. Use `valueText` for localized text such as "3 of 5 records imported". Progress is read-only, not a slider, and not a Meter for static scores, capacity, battery, or health values. Use Alert, Badge, or Toast for task outcomes.

Toast has separate static presentation and managed stack forms. Static Toast is presentation-only; managed actions and icon-only dismissal use Button variants. Managed actions stay beside the copy with primary treatment, while dismissal remains the trailing ghost control. Toast width is capped at 25rem (400px) before viewport insets reduce it on smaller screens, and the managed viewport is bottom inline-end. Collapsed cards scale and step upward behind the frontmost toast, then expand upward while preserving reading order. Use `ToastProvider`, `ToastViewport`, and `useToastManager` for transient application feedback. Duplicate IDs update in place, `timeout={0}` creates an intentionally persistent toast, low priority is polite, and high priority is reserved for urgent failures. Managed timers preserve remaining duration during hover, keyboard focus, or window blur. The viewport inherits document direction on the first interactive render, follows root `dir` changes, and resolves `inline-start` and `inline-end` for LTR or RTL; an explicit `direction` prop wins immediately. A unified enter, expand, swipe, and dismissal coordinate system preserves offsets in all four physical directions, including reduced motion. The viewport also supports safe areas, compact density, F6 keyboard entry, localized labels, and a dismiss button. Use one provider per stack; use `createToastManager` only when an independent second provider is intentional. Toast is not a notification inbox, persistent history, or background-job manager.

Toggle is a client-only Base UI Core action for one independent retained button state. Import it from `@nerio-ui/ui/client` or install editable source with `pnpm exec nerio add toggle`. It exposes `pressed`, `defaultPressed`, `onPressedChange`, `value`, `disabled`, `ghost` or `outline`, `sm` or `md` or `lg`, forwarded refs, and render composition. Icon-only usage requires a stable `aria-label`; visible-label usage accepts children and one leading Nerio icon. Keep the accessible name stable while `aria-pressed` communicates state. Use Button for momentary actions, Switch for immediate settings, Checkbox for selection, and ToggleGroup for grouped values and roving focus. Toggle does not own form-field semantics, loading, persistence, permissions, formatting, filters, or product policy.

ToggleGroup is a client-only Base UI grouped pressed-state control. Import it from `@nerio-ui/ui/client` or install editable source with `pnpm exec nerio add toggle-group`. It owns one controlled or uncontrolled string array in single or multiple mode, a required accessible group name, horizontal or vertical orientation, RTL-aware roving focus, disabled items, and options or ToggleGroupItem composition. It reuses Toggle variants and sizes. Tabs, RadioGroup, CheckboxGroup, MultiSelect, tags, filters, persistence, and product command policy remain separate responsibilities.

CheckboxGroup is a client-only Base UI grouped form control. Import it from `@nerio-ui/ui/client` or install editable source with `pnpm exec nerio add checkbox-group`. It owns one controlled or uncontrolled array of stable string values, a visible group label with optional description and message, shared name and form metadata, disabled and read-only group states, disabled items, item descriptions, options or CheckboxGroupItem composition, form submission, and uncontrolled native reset. Use it for a short visible set of independent options. RadioGroup owns one exclusive choice, ToggleGroup owns retained button states, and MultiSelect, tags, filters, persistence, remote data, and product workflows remain outside this primitive.

Input is a server-safe thin native control for `text`, `email`, `password`, `search`, `tel`, `url`, `number`, `date`, `month`, `week`, `time`, and `datetime-local` values. Use `size="sm" | "md" | "lg"`, use `htmlSize` for the native HTML size attribute, and compose labels, descriptions, and messages through `Field`. Temporal Input types preserve browser-owned pickers, localized chrome, native value strings, validity, direct form submission, and forwarded-ref access to `valueAsDate` where supported and `valueAsNumber`; `datetime-local` has no standard `valueAsDate` representation. Input does not own validation policy, visual prefix/suffix content, search results, password visibility, localized parsing, Calendar, DatePicker, scheduling, or timezone workflows. Use InputGroup for a shared Input surface with explicit `InputGroupAddon placement="start" | "end"`; addons do not provide the input's accessible name, and interactive addons remain independently accessible. FileInput is a server-safe native file-selection primitive. It fixes `type="file"`, rejects controlled `value` and `defaultValue`, forwards the native input ref and FileList events, supports `accept`, `capture`, `multiple`, `name`, `form`, `required`, `disabled`, and native form reset, and uses Field or native labels for naming. Browser picker chrome and security remain platform-owned. Upload requests, validation workflows, Dropzone, previews, queues, progress, retry, persistence, and storage remain consumer or Pro responsibilities. Slider is a client-only Base UI Core component for exactly one numeric value and one thumb. It requires one naming strategy through `label`, `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby`; supports controlled/uncontrolled value, min/max/step/largeStep, horizontal/vertical orientation, name/form/required/disabled/readOnly, root/input refs, and localized `aria-valuetext`; and preserves Base UI Arrow, Home, End, Page, pointer, touch, RTL, and form behavior. Use `valueLabel` only for consumer-formatted visible text. Multi-thumb ranges, marks, tooltips, charts, thresholds, filters, pricing, and media policy remain consumer or Pro responsibilities. Calendar is a client-only single-date Core grid with timezone-independent `YYYY-MM-DD` values. It requires `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`; supports controlled/uncontrolled selected date and visible month, inclusive min/max boundaries, a consumer `isDateDisabled` rule, locale-formatted month/weekday/day labels with an `en-US` default for deterministic SSR, explicit `firstDayOfWeek`, localized navigation labels, disabled/read-only states, and a stable `today` date for deterministic SSR. One day participates in the Tab sequence; Arrow keys move by day or week, Home/End move within a week, Page keys move by month, Shift plus Page keys move by year, and Enter/Space select. DatePicker composes the same single-date ISO contract with a form-backed field and Popover. Date ranges, scheduling, recurrence, events, availability, time and timezone conversion, upload workflows, presets, natural-language parsing, global/entity/advanced search, CommandPalette, and FilterBar remain consumer or Pro responsibilities. The canonical boundary is `docs/core-platform-primitive-coverage.md`.

Combobox is a client-only bounded single-select Core 1.1 primitive. Import it from `@nerio-ui/ui/client` or install editable source with `pnpm exec nerio add combobox`. Flat or grouped options require a stable generic string `value`, visible `label`, explicit searchable `textValue`, optional description, and optional disabled state; composed mode pairs the same canonical items with ComboboxItem and group children. Query, selected value, and popup state each have independent controlled and uncontrolled pairs. Default filtering uses locale-aware contains matching, `filter` accepts a synchronous consumer predicate, and `filter={false}` preserves a consumer-filtered list. Name, form, required, autoComplete, disabled, readOnly, form reset, clear, localized action labels, empty presentation, and loading presentation are supported. Core does not own remote fetching, debounce, ranking, creation, virtualization, multiple selection, tags, routing, analytics, persistence, or business validation. Use Select for a compact known set without query input and Command for actions rather than a selected form value.

MultiSelect is a client-only bounded Core 1.2 primitive. Import it from `@nerio-ui/ui/client` or install editable source with `pnpm exec nerio add multi-select`. Its options-only contract accepts flat or grouped finite local data with unique string values, visible labels, explicit searchable `textValue`, optional descriptions, and disabled state. Ordered selection, query, and popup state each have independent controlled and uncontrolled pairs. Removable text values wrap inside the field; selected disabled values remain visible and submitted but cannot be directly removed. Name emits repeated ordered form values, required means at least one known value, uncanceled reset restores uncontrolled defaults, and a permanently mounted polite region announces selection, removal, and clear-all. Every Core-owned action and announcement string is overridable through `labels`. Core does not own fetching, creation, free-form tags, virtualization, quotas, conditional availability, rich product chips, persistence, analytics, or FilterBar workflows. Use CheckboxGroup when a short set should remain visible and Combobox for one filtered value.

SearchField is a client-only native search composition. Import it from `@nerio-ui/ui/client` or install editable source with `pnpm exec nerio add search-field`. It owns one controlled or uncontrolled string query, a visible Field label with description/message relationships, an accessible localizable clear action that restores focus to the same input, an IME-safe Enter `onSearch` event that does not suppress native form submission, form/reset behavior, disabled/read-only/invalid states, autofill attributes, a decorative search-icon slot, and a localizable loading status or custom loading-indicator slot. Results, suggestions, requests, debounce, filtering, ranking, routing, global shortcuts, history, analytics, and product-specific search workflows remain consumer or Pro responsibilities. Use Input for a plain native field, Combobox for selecting one value from a bounded synchronous set, and Command for action-result navigation.

NumberField is a client-only Base UI Core 1.1 component for one decimal quantity. Import it from `@nerio-ui/ui/client` or install editable source with `pnpm exec nerio add number-field`. It supports controlled or uncontrolled `number | null` value, localized decimal parsing and formatting with a deterministic `en-US` default, finite min/max bounds, positive step/smallStep/largeStep values, deliberate keyboard and button stepping, change and commit reasons, visible Field relationships, native name/form/required/reset behavior, disabled/read-only/invalid states, localizable decrement/increment labels, and LTR/RTL layout. Wheel-driven changes are deliberately disabled. Currency and accounting policy, arbitrary parsing, unit conversion, calculations, business validation, product-specific steppers, and scrub interactions remain consumer or Pro responsibilities. Use Input for raw native numeric strings and Slider for choosing one value across a visually bounded range.

OTPField is a client-only Base UI Core 1.1 component for one short verification code. Import it from `@nerio-ui/ui/client` or install editable source with `pnpm exec nerio add otp-field`. It supports one controlled or uncontrolled string, a required positive length, numeric, alphabetic, or alphanumeric validation, deterministic typing, paste and deletion, one-time-code autofill, mobile keyboard hints, name/form/required/reset behavior, disabled/read-only/invalid states, localizable positional slot labels, concise associated messages, and a completion callback. Its visual separator is hidden from assistive technology, and one hidden input submits the complete code. Authentication requests, verification, resend, countdowns, masking, rate limits, recovery workflows, and credential storage remain consumer responsibilities.

Nerio Core uses Tailwind CSS v4-first component authoring while `--n-*` variables remain the canonical visual value layer. Package consumers import `@nerio-ui/tokens/tailwind.css` and explicitly register `@nerio-ui/ui/src` with Tailwind `@source`; source-installed TSX is detected from the consumer project. Nerio packages do not inject Tailwind Preflight. All Core components use this contract; residual CSS is limited to named keyframes plus scoped Nerio-class box sizing and native-control font inheritance for consumers without Preflight.

Supported package consumers use Node.js >=22, React >=19 <20, Next.js >=16.2.0 <17, TypeScript >=5.9 <6, and Tailwind CSS >=4.1.0 <5. Packed compatibility evidence covers a minimum stack on Node 22 and the current stack on Node 22 and Node 24. The pinned Playwright 1.62.1 release gate covers Chromium 151+, Firefox 153+, and WebKit 26.5+ across documentation and docs-local Template routes. Exact safe-area inset and forced-colors emulation remain Chromium-specific automated evidence; assistive-technology and real-device coverage is tracked as a manual release gate.

AI agents should select the smallest component set that matches the workflow, avoid unnecessary domain-specific assumptions in Core, use Pro for advanced product workflows, keep examples universal unless the task explicitly asks for a vertical, and never introduce shadcn/ui, Radix UI, Headless UI, Ariakit, or overlapping primitive libraries.

The public Blocks catalog is available at `/blocks`. Its nine docs-local compositions cover sign in,
account creation, password recovery, profile settings, security settings, notification preferences,
a basic table toolbar, an account summary, and deterministic file-upload states.
Each catalog card navigates in the same tab to its same-origin `/views/blocks/[slug]` preview, which
provides a `Back to Blocks` action for returning to the catalog. Blocks solve one bounded task; they
are not Templates, Core component APIs, complete application shells, or backend workflows.
